H10_CERTIFICATE.pointwise_hunter_inequality: For every outcome, the subgraph induced by its present residual events is a forest with at most max(m-1, 0) edges. Thus the union indicator is bounded by the sum of event indicators minus the sum of intersection indicators on the selected tree.

threshold_minimum.universal_argument:
Adopt Paired Root for 150 sealed members, including all 170 vectors.

Every event is R_i = E_i minus (E_A union E_B). Pair counts below are
residual intersections, recounted by cell-count dynamic programming and
inclusion-exclusion; no official-outcome enumeration is needed.

For n type-0 events, 6n incidences occupy 40 outside labels. Smoothing
a>=b+2 to a-1,b+1 decreases sum C(d,2) by a-b-1. The balanced minimum Q
therefore bounds the collision mass e1+e2+e3. A graph with component ranks
r_j has e<=sum C(r_j+1,2)<=C(sum r_j+1,2), so rank>=rho(e).
Descending Kruskal spans all nested threshold graphs simultaneously.
One common core tree thus weighs at least
(n-1)phi0 + sum (phi_j-phi_{j-1})rho(e_j).

Select any core vertex as root and attach each omitted event once as a
new leaf. Core and attachment edges are disjoint; there are 18 vertices
and 17 distinct edges. Each legal residual root pair has its type-specific
floor, so core and leaf floors add ON THIS SAME TREE. For each outcome
with m present events, the induced tree is a forest with at most m-1
edges (zero if m=0). Consequently 1_union <= sum 1_R - sum_tree 1_pair
pointwise, proving the universal Hunter inequality by integration.

Different certificates combine by MAX, with one subtraction. Every
compressed member MAXes all represented-vector safe bounds. Predecessor
certificates are consumed as immutable data, never rebuilt or readopted.

tree_extension.universal_argument:
Adopt H11/H16 for fourteen members after the sealed H13 adoption.

Events are residual: R_i = E_i minus (E_A union E_B). For n type-0
events the 6n outside incidences occupy 40 labels. Smoothing a>=b+2 to
a-1,b+1 decreases sum C(d,2) by a-b-1, proving the balanced collision
floor for every support. Double counting gives sum C(d,2)=e1+e2+e3.
For threshold-graph component ranks r_j, e<=sum C(r_j+1,2)
<=C(sum r_j+1,2); hence rank>=rho(e). Descending Kruskal spans each
nested threshold graph simultaneously, giving ONE common core tree with
weight >= (n-1)phi0 + sum_j (phi_j-phi_{j-1})rho(e_j).

For any outcome with m present events, the induced subgraph of a tree is
a forest with at most m-1 edges (zero for m=0). Thus
1_union <= sum 1_R - sum_tree 1_intersection pointwise for all supports.
Integrating proves Hunter. Attach each omitted event once as a new leaf
to a core root: n-1 + 18-n = 17 distinct edges on 18 vertices. Every
residual intersection is a set cardinality and nonnegative. Only the core
credit is used; no positive attachment floor is assumed.

Existing credits combine by MAX and are subtracted once. Compressed
members MAX all represented-vector bounds. All other sealed bounds and
all Classified/Tail terms survive unchanged. No predecessor construction,
census, solver, or official-outcome enumeration is invoked.
